messages.body: Alex, can you share the sprint velocity numbers from last quarter?
Sure, let me pull them from Jira. Give me a moment.
Q3 average was 42 story points per sprint. We had one outlier sprint at 28 due to the incident in October.
That's useful context. I'll adjust the Q4 forecast accordingly.
Sounds good. Let me know if you need the breakdown by team or epic.
Hey Alex! Got a sec to review the Q4 roadmap doc I sent over?
Sure, give me 10 minutes. Just finishing up a standup.
No rush! The main thing I want your eyes on is the resource allocation section.
OK looked at it. I think we're understaffing the infra work. We should add at least 1 more engineer.
Agreed. I'll flag it to Jamie in the planning meeting today.
Also — are you going to the all-hands on Thursday?
Alex, I wanted to loop you in on something. We're kicking off the CI/CD pipeline migration project next sprint.
The goal is to move everything from Jenkins to GitHub Actions. It's been on the backlog for over a year.
We have 47 pipeline jobs currently. Some are trivial, but a few have custom Groovy scripts that are going to be a pain to port.
I started an audit spreadsheet. The high-risk jobs are the ones touching the deploy-to-prod pipeline and the nightly test regression suite.
Do you think we should do a parallel-run period where both Jenkins and GHA run simultaneously for 2 weeks before cutover?
The concern is that GHA has a 6-hour job timeout limit — some of our nightly runs take 7+ hours on Jenkins.
One option is to break those long jobs into matrix strategies with parallelism. But that means re-architecting the test suite.
I also need to cost out GitHub Actions usage. We're currently on the free tier for our private repos — this migration will bump us to Team plan at minimum.
Alex, can you sign off on the project charter? I need it to pull in Morgan and Quinn for the implementation.
The charter is in Confluence under Eng/Projects/CI-CD-Migration. I've already gotten buy-in from the SRE team.
Also want to flag that the Jenkins server contract renewal is in March. If we don't migrate by then we're auto-renewed for another year.
That's a $48k/year license we'd love to not pay for if we can hit the migration target.
One more thing — I'm thinking of setting up a migration guild with a weekly sync. Would you be willing to sponsor the initiative from the leadership side?
I know it's a lot to drop on you at once. Let me know when you have 20 min to walk through everything together.
Oh and I should mention — Avery has already started benchmarking GHA runner performance vs Jenkins agents on the same workloads. Results are looking promising.
Avery's benchmarks show ~30% faster job execution on GHA for the standard build jobs. Security scanning is the same speed.
That should help the ROI argument when we present to the VP of Eng. Let me know your thoughts, Alex!
Morgan, did you finish the API migration notes?
Almost done. There are a few edge cases around the auth token refresh I'm still documenting.
Take your time. We don't need it until EOD Friday.
Perfect, I'll have it to you by Thursday latest. Should I drop it in the shared Drive or send directly?
Drop it in Drive please, under the Engineering/Docs/Migrations folder.
Taylor, quick question on the budget projections. Did finance approve the extra headcount?
Not yet. They want to see the ROI model first. I'm working on it with Priya.
When do you think you'll have a draft ready?
Hopefully by end of next week. It's a bit complex because we have to account for contractor vs FTE costs.
Actually Alex I've been doing more thinking on the headcount ROI model and I need to walk you through the full picture.
We're requesting 3 new FTE engineers for the platform team. Total fully-loaded cost is roughly $900k/year.
Finance wants a 3-year NPV justification. I modeled it out and the break-even is at around 18 months based on productivity gains.
The productivity gain assumptions are based on reducing on-call burden, faster deploys, and unblocking 2 feature teams who are currently bottlenecked on platform work.
I assumed 15% feature team velocity improvement post-platform investment. That's conservative — Shopify reported 22% in a similar case study.
One complication: Finance is insisting on a contractor comparison. I need your input on whether we should do FTE or use contractors for the first 6 months.
My recommendation is FTE from day 1. Contractors would save ~$120k year 1 but cost more long-term due to ramp time and knowledge transfer overhead.
Also the platform work is highly contextual — contractors would struggle without deep internal knowledge of our infra stack.
Alex, can you send me your team's current on-call load stats? I need the average pages/week per engineer for the model.
Also need the deployment frequency data for the last 6 months — how many deploys/week and what % require manual intervention.
I'll plug those into the model. Once the draft is done I'll need your sign-off before it goes to the VP of Engineering.
The VP meeting is scheduled for next Tuesday at 3pm. We have 30 minutes to make the case.
I'm also planning to include a hiring timeline: JD posted by Week 2, interviews in Week 4-6, offers in Week 7, start dates in Week 10.
That timeline is aggressive. Do you think recruiting can move that fast? Last time we hired platform engineers it took 14 weeks.
We might want to float the idea of internal transfers as a faster option for at least 1 of the 3 positions.
Casey mentioned they'd be interested in moving to platform. You'd know better than me if that's a good fit.
Alex — bottom line: I need your data inputs by EOD tomorrow and your sign-off on the charter by Friday. Can you confirm you can hit those?
This is the biggest investment ask the engineering org has made in 2 years. Really appreciate your support on it.
Alex, are you joining the UX review session today at 3pm?
Yes! I just accepted the calendar invite. Looking forward to seeing the new designs.
Great! We're focusing on the onboarding flow today. Lot of changes based on the last user research round.
I heard the drop-off rate at step 3 was really high. Curious what the new approach is.
Yeah it was brutal — 68% drop-off. The new design consolidates steps 3 and 4 and adds inline help text.
Hey Alex — I finished the compliance audit report. Want me to walk you through the findings?
That would be great. Can we do it tomorrow morning?
Sure. How does 9am work?
9am is good. I'll send a calendar invite.
There's one critical finding you should know about before then — we have a gap in our data retention policy for GDPR.
Alex, I know it's late but I need to brief you on the full compliance audit before tomorrow's meeting.
We found 5 significant gaps. I'm going to walk through each one here so you have context going into the meeting.
Gap 1: Data retention. We're keeping user PII for an indefinite period in the analytics database. GDPR requires a maximum 13-month retention for marketing analytics data.
Gap 2: Right to erasure. Our current data deletion flow only removes users from the primary DB. It doesn't cascade to the data warehouse, audit logs, or backups.
Gap 3: Consent logging. We don't have a versioned audit trail for when users accepted/updated their consent. This is critical for demonstrating compliance in an audit.
Gap 4: Data portability. We have no mechanism for users to export their data in a machine-readable format. Article 20 of GDPR requires this.
Gap 5: Third-party processor agreements. We have 3 vendors processing EU user data without current DPAs in place — one of them handles payment tokenization.
Gaps 1, 2, and 5 are the most urgent. A regulator visit today would be a problem for all three.
Alex, this is going to need engineering resourcing to fix. Estimated effort: Gap 1 = 3 sprints, Gap 2 = 2 sprints, Gap 3 = 1 sprint, Gap 4 = 2 sprints, Gap 5 = mostly legal + 0.5 sprint.
I've already drafted a remediation roadmap with prioritization. I'll share it in the meeting but wanted you to have the headline numbers first.
The legal team has been looped in. They're concerned about the DPA situation and want to know if we can fast-track those vendor agreements.
One of the vendors (Helios Payments) has been unresponsive to our legal team for 3 weeks. We may need to escalate or consider switching providers.
Switching payment processors mid-year would be a major engineering effort — probably 4-5 sprints. I don't think we should rule it out though given the compliance risk.
I'll need you to help call for a decision from leadership on the Helios situation. This is above my level to decide unilaterally.
In summary: we're exposed on multiple GDPR fronts. I'd classify our overall posture as 'medium-high risk' right now.
The good news is all gaps are fixable with focused effort over the next 2 quarters. Nothing that requires a full platform overhaul.
See you at 9am Alex. Bring coffee — it's going to be a dense session.
PS — I've also flagged a potential CCPA concern for our California users. I'll cover that at the end if we have time.
Avery, thanks for leading the incident postmortem yesterday. Really smooth facilitation.
Thanks! It was a tough one — 4 hours of downtime is never fun to dig through. But the team was great.
Agreed. Are the action items tracked somewhere?
Yes — I added them all to the Jira board under the P0-postmortem epic. 7 action items total, 3 are high priority.
Perfect. Let's do a weekly check-in on those until they're all resolved.
Alex, I pushed the hotfix to staging. Can you do a quick smoke test?
On it. Give me 5 minutes.
Tested. Login flow and checkout both look good. The payment error is fixed.
Great, I'll promote to prod now. Thanks for the quick turnaround!
No problem. Let me know once it's live and I'll monitor the error rates.
Sam, are you taking point on the vendor evaluation this quarter?
Yes, I'm coordinating with procurement. We have three vendors shortlisted so far.
Which three are you looking at?
Datadog, New Relic, and Grafana Cloud. Each has different pricing and feature tradeoffs.
I've been running a deeper analysis over the past few days. Here's where I've landed — full breakdown below.
Datadog: Best-in-class APM and distributed tracing. Excellent Kubernetes integration. Pricing is the highest — estimated $180k/year at our scale.
Datadog pros: unified platform (metrics, logs, traces, dashboards), great alerting, strong community. Cons: expensive, vendor lock-in is real.
New Relic: Good all-around platform, pricing is per-user which works in our favor since we have a small ops team. Estimated $95k/year.
New Relic cons: their UI has improved but is still not as polished as Datadog. Their Kubernetes dashboards are behind.
Grafana Cloud: Open source stack (Prometheus + Loki + Tempo). Cheapest option — estimated $40k/year. But requires more operational overhead.
Grafana Cloud pros: no vendor lock-in, data stays in our infra, highly customizable. Cons: team needs to manage alerts, dashboards, and retention config ourselves.
My recommendation: Grafana Cloud if we can allocate 0.5 FTE to platform observability work. Otherwise Datadog is worth the cost for the productivity gains.
Alex, I know you've been pushing for Grafana to keep costs down. I want to make sure we're realistic about the maintenance burden.
Quinn did a POC with Datadog last week. Said the auto-instrumentation for our Node.js services took 2 hours vs 2 days with Grafana.
I've also run numbers for a hybrid approach: Grafana for infra metrics (cheap) + Datadog just for APM. Comes out to ~$90k/year.
The hybrid approach is operationally more complex but gives us the best of both worlds on cost vs capability.
I need a decision by end of this week. Procurement needs 3 weeks lead time to negotiate contract terms before Q1 end.
Can we set up a 30-min call today or tomorrow to align? I'll prepare a one-pager for you to share with the leadership team.
Also — separate topic — the current on-prem monitoring setup (Nagios + Grafana OSS) is becoming a liability. Server is running on hardware from 2019 and is out of support warranty.
If that server goes down we're flying blind. It happened once last year and it was not fun. We need to decommission it regardless of which vendor we choose.
Alex, I've put together all the data. Whatever direction you want to go, I'll support it. But we really can't punt on this decision any longer.
The comparison matrix is in the shared Drive under Eng/Infra/Observability-Eval-2024. Let me know when you've had a chance to review.
Hey Alex, wanted to introduce myself — I'm Drew, joining the growth team next Monday.
Welcome Drew! Great to connect. Looking forward to working with you.
Thanks! Could you walk me through the onboarding process? I wasn't sure who to reach out to first.
Sure! I'll schedule a 30-minute intro call for Monday afternoon. I'll also add you to the relevant channels.
That sounds perfect. Really appreciate the warm welcome!
Team — I've drafted the OKRs for Q1. Can everyone review by EOD Wednesday?
I'll review. One heads up — I think we need to revisit the reliability KR, it's too vague.
Agree with Morgan. We should tie it to a specific SLA target like 99.9% uptime.
Makes sense. Let's use 99.9% as the baseline. I'll propose that on the doc.
Team — new topic. I want to propose we adopt a service mesh this quarter. I've been evaluating Istio and Linkerd.
Context: we now have 34 microservices in production. Managing mTLS, retries, and circuit breakers at the app level is becoming painful.
A service mesh would give us: automatic mTLS everywhere, observability (traces + metrics per service pair), and traffic shaping without code changes.
I've looked at Istio before. The control plane overhead is non-trivial. Are we sure we need the full feature set?
Fair point Morgan. Linkerd is much lighter — it adds about 2ms per hop vs Istio's 8-10ms. For our latency-sensitive services that matters.
What's the ops burden for running a service mesh? Who on the team would own it?
The SRE team would own it — that's us. I've been researching this too and I think Linkerd is the right call. Simpler ops story.
If we go Linkerd, what's the migration path? Do we instrument all 34 services at once or roll it out progressively?
Progressive rollout. Start with the payment and auth services (highest risk / highest value), then expand from there.
I can scope the payment service integration. It's our most complex from a mTLS standpoint — if Linkerd handles it we're good for the rest.
Let's set up a dedicated design doc. I'll create a skeleton in Confluence and share it in this channel by EOD.
This sounds promising. Alex here — I'm supportive but want us to be honest about the risk. Service meshes can be a footgun if not owned well.
Agreed Alex. We'll include a rollback plan in the design doc and require approval from you and the SRE lead before each phase.
I'd also recommend we do a load test comparing baseline vs mesh-injected traffic before any production rollout.
+1 to Morgan's suggestion. I'll add that as a required gate in the design doc.
Also worth noting — Linkerd just released v2.14 last week with improved multi-cluster support. That's relevant for our EU/US split.
Great catch Avery. I'll include v2.14 in the evaluation. The multi-cluster story is key for us if we ever want to do active-active.
One more consideration: do we have the Kubernetes RBAC configured to support Linkerd's injection webhook? That tripped up another team I know.
I'll check the cluster RBAC config this afternoon. Quinn on it.
Design doc skeleton is up in Confluence: Engineering > Architecture > Service Mesh Proposal 2024. Review and comment by Friday.
Alex, can you add your thoughts on the risk tolerance section? That part needs an EM perspective.
Reminder: sprint planning is tomorrow at 10am. Please come with your top 3 priorities for the backlog.
Quick question — are we including the accessibility backlog items this sprint?
Yes, at least 2 accessibility items per our Q1 commitment. They're already tagged in Jira.
I'll add my priorities to the sheet now. Are we using the same Google Sheet as last sprint?
Yes, same sheet. I added a new tab for this sprint.
ALERT: Detection system showing elevated error rate on the payment service. Spike started ~10 minutes ago.
On it. Checking the logs now. Looks like it started after the last deployment.
I'm rolling back the deployment as a precaution.
Good call. I'll draft comms for the status page. Keep me posted on ETA to resolution.
Rollback complete. Error rate dropping now.
Confirmed — error rate back to baseline. Monitoring for next 30 minutes.
Good work everyone. Root cause appears to be a null pointer in the new payment validation logic.
I'll create a Jira ticket for the fix and schedule a postmortem for tomorrow.
Alex — incident resolved. Total duration: 32 minutes. No data loss.
Here are the incident tickets created for the postmortem follow-ups.
Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow at 2pm. All team members please attend.
Postmortem done. 5 action items identified. Sharing the full report now.
Action item 1: Add null-check guard in PaymentValidationService.validate() — owner: Quinn, due: next sprint.
Action item 2: Add integration test coverage for null payment method scenario — owner: Morgan, due: next sprint.
Action item 3: Improve deployment canary strategy — currently we deploy 100% instantly. We need a 5%/25%/100% rollout with automated rollback triggers.
I'll take action item 3. I've been wanting to implement Argo Rollouts for this. The canary strategy is long overdue.
Action item 4: Set up a synthetic monitoring probe for the payment service that fires before real users are affected.
Action item 5: Define and document a formal SEV-1 escalation runbook so we don't have to improvise during incidents.
I'll draft the SEV-1 runbook this week. I have a template from my previous company I can adapt.
Alex — we want your input on action item 3 scope. Argo Rollouts would be great but it's a new dependency. Do you think the team is ready to operate it?
Also worth flagging: this is the third payment service incident in 4 months. We should consider a dedicated reliability sprint focused on that service.
Agreed with Sam. The payment service has accumulated significant tech debt. A reliability sprint would give us the runway to address it properly.
Alex can you add a reliability sprint to the Q1 planning agenda? I think we have a strong case now after 3 incidents.
Full postmortem doc is now in Confluence: Engineering > Incidents > INC-2024-003. Please review and add your timeline contributions.
Welcome to Q1 2024 everyone! We're kicking off a new initiative to improve developer tooling this quarter.
Exciting! This has been a long time coming. Looking forward to seeing what the team comes up with.
Reminder: all-hands meeting is this Thursday at 2pm. Please add your agenda items to the shared doc.
Also a reminder that the new performance review cycle opens next Monday. Managers will send calendar invites.
Congrats to the product team for shipping the new dashboard! Great collaboration across the org.
Anyone else see that the office coffee machine has been upgraded? Game changer.
Yes!! The oat milk frother is elite. I'm already on my third cup.
What's everyone's lunch plans today? Thinking of hitting the new ramen place nearby.
I'm in! What time are you heading over?
Was thinking 12:30. Anyone else want to join?
I'll come too! I've been curious about that place since they opened.
Count me in. Does anyone know if it's a cash-only spot?
It's card/contactless only actually. Checked their site.
I can't make it today — deep in postmortem action items. Save me a bowl?
Ha, ramen doesn't travel well Quinn. Next time!
Also — anyone going to the tech meetup tonight? There's a talk on platform engineering at the downtown venue.
I was planning to! The speaker did a great blog post on Kubernetes failure domains last year.
Which venue? I might come if it's not too far from the office.
It's at the Foundry on 4th. Doors open at 6:30, talk starts at 7. Free entry.
I'll come. Sounds like a good way to wind down after a chaotic week 😂
Ha agreed. Also — random but I found an amazing VS Code extension that auto-generates JSDoc comments from function signatures. Saving me so much time.
Is this the AI one? I've been experimenting with Copilot for that but the quality is inconsistent.
Yeah it's AI-powered. Not perfect but it's solid 80% of the time and saves a ton of boilerplate.
I've been using Copilot for a few months now. Once you learn to treat it as a fast autocomplete rather than a solution generator, it's pretty useful.
Alex that's a great framing. I was getting frustrated with it generating wrong logic but you're right — it's better for boilerplate.
Hot take: AI coding assistants are great until the code review. Then you realize you don't fully understand what you shipped 😅
Sam speaking from personal experience there. We've all been there.
Haha too real. OK I'm leaving for the ramen place now. See the lunch crew there!
